meta.title: ExperimentLens — Visual analytics & explainability for ML experiments
meta.description: An extensible visual analytics dashboard for ML experiments. Plug in your tracker and your execution engine, then compare runs, inspect data, and explain models — all in one UI.

hero.subtitle:
ExperimentLens is a lightweight yet powerful visual dashboard for the interactive exploration, monitoring, and explainability of complex AI pipelines.
Developed within the context of the ExtremeXP project, ExperimentLens empowers researchers, data scientists, and engineers to make sense of experimental results across multiple runs and interconnected tasks.
hero.imageAlt: ExperimentLens overview dashboard with parallel coordinates plot across 108 runs
hero.imageCaption: ExperimentLens dashboard: analyzing configuration effects on experiment performance.

valueProps.title: A single lens over your entire ML experimentation loop.
valueProps.subtitle: From orchestration to explanation — without leaving the browser.

items.title: Tracker- & engine-agnostic
items.body: Adapter interface to MLflow today, with Kubeflow as the execution engine. Airflow and other backends are on the roadmap.

items.title: Visual analytics, not just tables
items.body: Parallel coordinates, comparative metric views, group-by, filters and color encodings — designed to make 100s of runs legible at a glance.

items.title: Explainability built-in
items.body: Feature importance, Partial Dependence (PDP), Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) and counterfactual views wired directly to your runs.

featuresPreview.title: Built for the whole experiment lifecycle.
featuresPreview.subtitle: From first run to final explanation — everything in one UI.

integrations.title: Works with the stack you already run.
integrations.subtitle: ExperimentLens consumes runs from your tracker and orchestrates them through your engine.

cards.name: MLflow
cards.body: Logs runs, parameters, metrics and artifacts. ExperimentLens reads MLflow experiments directly so every visualization, comparison and explanation maps back to a real MLflow run.

cards.name: Kubeflow
cards.body: Runs the underlying pipelines on Kubernetes. ExperimentLens surfaces Kubeflow pipeline executions as first-class workflows you can inspect, compare and explain.

integrations.footnote: Adapter-based design — additional trackers and engines (e.g. Airflow) can be added without changing the UI.

howItWorks.title: From pipeline to insight in three steps.

steps.title: Orchestrate
steps.body: Author your experiment as an execution engine pipeline. ExperimentLens picks it up as a first-class workflow.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: Each run logs parameters, metrics and artifacts to the tracker — automatically surfaced in the dashboard.

steps.title: Explore & explain
steps.body: Compare runs visually, drill into artifacts and apply explainability methods without leaving the UI.

demoStrip.title: See it on a real experiment.
demoStrip.subtitle: A public deployment running a 108-run fairness experiment.

repos.title: Three repositories, one platform.
repos.subtitle: ExperimentLens is developed in the open within the ExtremeXP project.
